Five Apple Watch models can measure your blood pressure and alert you when you may be developing high blood pressure, but they don't provide actual blood pressure readings.

Some smart rings and other fitness devices can do this, but they require periodic calibration with a traditional upper-arm blood pressure monitor. The upcoming Signal Ring claims to offer full blood pressure measurement without any calibration, citing clinical trials involving thousands of people…

"Silent killer"

Abnormally high blood pressure (hypertension) and abnormally low blood pressure (hypotension) both carry serious health risks.

Of the two, hypertension is more dangerous, earning the nickname "silent killer" because it can cause severe, irreversible damage to your arteries, heart and brain without obvious symptoms. Many people only discover they have the condition after suffering a heart attack or stroke.

For older adults, regular blood pressure monitoring is ideal. Home upper-arm blood pressure monitors are widely available and easy to use. But it would be even better if a fitness device worn daily could provide fully automatic monitoring.

Apple Watch blood pressure feature

With the launch of watchOS 26, five Apple Watch models can now measure blood pressure:

  • Apple Watch Series 11
  • Apple Watch Series 10
  • Apple Watch Series 9
  • Apple Watch Ultra 3
  • Apple Watch Ultra 2

However, these models won't give you any readings—they only issue alerts when they detect possible signs of hypertension. Other devices such as the Oura Ring work in a similar way.

Some fitness devices on the market can provide actual blood pressure readings, but require periodic calibration using measurements from an upper-arm blood pressure monitor.

Signal Ring

Startup Vital Signals says its Signal Ring smart ring can match the accuracy of a traditional upper-arm blood pressure monitor without any calibration.

CEO Tom Moss told Bloomberg that he nearly died from undiagnosed high blood pressure—an experience that inspired him to found the company.

The Signal Ring opens for pre-order later today, ships in October, and is priced at $399 with no subscription required. The companion app displays real-time blood pressure readings and long-term trends (as shown above).

Worth noting: the Oura Ring has not yet received approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), but clinical trials have shown it can deliver accurate blood pressure readings for thousands of participants.

Interestingly, Moss isn't particularly interested in marketing the Signal Ring to all consumers. He says the feature is best suited for older adults and people assessed by doctors as being at risk of hypertension—the implication being that the Signal Ring may not be especially outstanding in other areas (such as sleep tracking).
